title: Defense-in-depth annotated diagram: VPC, firewall, mTLS, RBAC v2, and SIEM exports
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a hardened private-deploy network pattern focused on: VPC segmentation, multilayer firewall rules, mutual TLS for service-to-service auth, RBAC v2 mapping for control plane and data plane, audit-log schema for evidentiary exports, and an evidence automation pipeline that feeds SIEM (Elastic/Splunk). Intended audience: SREs, infra engineers, security, and solution engineers prepping customer Private deployments.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to customer-managed VPCs and Redwood Private appliance deployments (VPC + optional on-prem bundle).
- Assumes central control plane has a private connectivity channel (VPN/PrivateLink) to customer VPCs and that customers can provision route tables and security groups.
- Focus is on network/data-plane controls + telemetry; host hardening and OS baselines are covered in separate OS-level docs.

High level defense-in-depth summary (short):
1) Perimeter: cloud provider routing + VPC peering/PrivateLink with small allowed CIDRs to control hops.
2) Network segmentation: three primary subnets per AZ: infra (control plane / management), inference (GPU pods), and customer-egress (ingress/proxy).
3) L4/L7 firewall rules: allow only required ports between segments; enforce TLS termination at proxy with mTLS preserved between services where possible.
4) mTLS for service-to-service auth with short-lived certs and automated rotation.
5) RBAC v2 enforces who/what can call control plane APIs and what model routes are allowed.
6) Audit schema records policy decisions, cert details, token IDs; regular SIEM exports and signed evidence blobs are produced for compliance.

Annotated ASCII diagram (single-AZ simplified):

  Internet --> LB (TLS termination) [public subnet]
                 |
                 v
         Ingress Proxy (mTLS client cert bridging) [customer-egress subnet]
           |         |           |
           |         |           v
           |         |   Control Plane API (private link) [infra subnet]
           |         v
    Inference (GPU pods) <-- internal L7 proxy (mTLS) [inference subnet]
          |
          v
   Local KV cache / prefix cache (encrypted at rest) [storage subnet]

Notes on diagram: LB only accepts TLS from customer egress IPs by allowlist; ingress proxy validates inbound client cert chains for enterprise customers who opt-in (mutual TLS). Internal traffic between inference pods and the control plane uses mTLS with certs issued by internal PKI.

VPC layout and subnet policy (recommended):
- infra-subnet: CIDR /24 per AZ. Hosts: control-plane APIs, management, SRE bastions (bastion only via restricted jump hosts). No public IPs.
- inference-subnet: smaller /24s with strict egress rules; only allowed to talk to infra-subnet on specific ports and to storage endpoints (S3 endpoints/NFS).
- customer-egress-subnet: public-facing NAT+proxy layer; allow inbound only on 443 from customer ingress CIDRs.
- storage-subnet: restricted, with logging endpoint service endpoints only.

Firewall / SG examples (cloud-agnostic pseudocode):
1) Ingress LB SG (public):
   - allow tcp:443 from customer_ingress_cidrs -> LB
   - deny all else
2) Ingress proxy SG:
   - allow tcp:8443 from LB
   - allow tcp:22 from infra-subnet (for debug jumps, logged)
   - egress tcp:443 to control-plane-api on specific ports
3) Control plane API SG:
   - allow tcp:7443 from ingress-proxy
   - allow tcp:7443 from infra-admin-bastion-ip (management)
   - allow tcp:9300 for internal metrics only from observability collectors
4) Inference pod SG (example K8s NetworkPolicy style):
   - ingress from internal-proxy on 8060-8070
   - egress to storage endpoints (S3) port 443
   - deny pod-to-pod egress unless labeled same-tenant=true

Example iptables/nft snippet (for on-prem agents):
# allow inbound from control plane
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -s 10.10.0.0/24 --dport 7443 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
# allow egress to storage
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 10.20.0.0/24 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
# default drop
iptables -P INPUT DROP
iptables -P OUTPUT DROP

mTLS design and operational patterns:
- PKI: Internal intermediate CA signing short-lived leaf certs (TTL 8 hours recommended for workload certs; rotation window 6 hours). Root CA securely stored in HSM/KMS.
- Certificates delivered via an internal cert-distribution service that integrates with workload identity (pod service account or instance identity). Use SPIFFE IDs for workload identity where possible.
- Verification: both client and server perform cert-chain validation + check CRL/OCSP status from the internal OCSP responder.
- Mutual auth decisions must be captured in the audit log (cert_serial, spiffe_id, validation_result).
- Rotations: rolling rotation orchestrated via controller; fallback path uses cached key material to avoid outages for stale certificates.

Operational checklist for mTLS rollout:
- [ ] Deploy internal PKI and OCSP responder behind infra-subnet.
- [ ] Configure cert-distribution controller in each cluster/VM cluster with RBAC-limited service account.
- [ ] Enable short TTL leaf cert issuance and verify automated rotation works in staging (simulate CA outage and restore)
- [ ] Integrate verification results into the central audit stream (see Audit schema below)
- [ ] Document emergency key recovery and rotation runbook (include HSM steps)

RBAC v2 mapping (control + data plane):
- Concepts: principal (human or service), role, scope (global, customer, cluster, namespace), resource type (models, routes, deployments, keys), action (read/list/start/stop/deploy), constraint (time window, source IP).
- Example roles:
  - infra-admin: manage infra, rotate certs, view full logs (requires MFA + SSO group).
  - model-deployer: can deploy model versions to a customer's dedicated pool (scope: customerX).
  - observability-reader: read-only access to metrics and traces (no access to secrets).
- Policy example (flattened sentence form):
  "role=model-deployer;principal=service:ci-cd@redwood;scope=customer:acme;resource=models/*;action=deploy;condition=source_ip in 10.10.0.0/24;ttl=8h"
- Enforcement points: API gateway enforces RBAC decisions for control plane; sidecar enforces decisions at data-plane for admin operations (e.g., start/stop GPU agents).

Audit log schema (JSON lines, required fields):
- timestamp: RFC3339 UTC string
- event_id: uuid4
- request_id: uuid4 (correlates distributed traces)
- principal: string (spiffe:// or user email)
- principal_type: user|service|machine
- action: string (e.g., models.deploy, network.connect)
- resource: string (resource type + id)
- decision: allow|deny|deferred
- decision_reason: short string
- src_ip: ip
- dst_ip: ip
- cert_serial: string (optional)
- mtls_verified: true|false
- rbac_policy_id: string (policy id that produced decision)
- token_id: string (if token used)
- request_payload_hash: sha256 hex
- response_status: http status or internal code
- duration_ms: number as string
- collector_id: string (which host/agent sent event)
- signature: base64 (optional, for evidence blobs)

Example audit line:
{"timestamp":"2026-02-19T21:14:12Z","event_id":"b3f2c6d8-...","request_id":"a1b2c3-...","principal":"spiffe://infra/agent-12","principal_type":"service","action":"models.start","resource":"deployment/rdw-gpu-42","decision":"allow","decision_reason":"cached-allow","src_ip":"10.1.4.12","dst_ip":"10.1.8.3","cert_serial":"308203...","mtls_verified":"true","rbac_policy_id":"rbac-v2-42","token_id":"tok-9f3a","request_payload_hash":"e3b0c4...","response_status":"202","duration_ms":"132","collector_id":"collector-eu-1"}

SIEM export design (push + pull hybrid):
- Primary export: collectors (filebeat/agent or rsyslog) pick up JSONL audit streams and push to central Elastic cluster or Splunk HEC. Configure TLS + HMAC on HEC endpoints.
- Secondary export: periodic signed evidence blobs (gzipped JSONL) stored in S3-compatible bucket with object metadata: {signed_by, time_window, sha256}. Manifest is signed by HSM-backed key.
- Retention: default 90 days hot, 2 years cold (customer-configurable). Evidence blobs kept 7 years for regulated customers.

SIEM mapping examples:
- Elastic ingest pipeline: parse timestamp -> ecs mapping: source.ip -> src_ip, destination.ip -> dst_ip, user.name -> principal
- Splunk HEC token mapping: index=redwood_private_audit sourcetype=redwood:audit

Example Splunk SPL quick-checks:
- High-failure mTLS attempts (last 24h):
  index=redwood_private_audit mtls_verified=false | stats count by principal, dst_ip | sort -count
- RBAC denies by policy:
  index=redwood_private_audit decision=deny | stats count by rbac_policy_id, principal

Evidence automation pipeline (sketch):
1) Local collector rotates write-ahead audit files every 15min into /var/lib/redwood/audit/ and pushes to local agent.
2) Agent validates JSON schema, signs batch with node key, uploads to staging S3 bucket with metadata.
3) Central verifier pulls manifests, verifies signatures with HSM public key, moves payload to SIEM queue and writes manifest entry to evidence-index (immutable ledger entry).
4) On confirmed delivery, agents mark local files archived and start retention timer.

Automation runbook for evidence collection (short):
- Ensure node clocks are NTP-synced (critical)
- Validate collector certs weekly via job that hits OCSP endpoint
- Run random sample verification job daily: pull 1% of manifests and re-verify signature and hash
- Run restore drill quarterly: restore evidence blob and replay to isolated SIEM instance to validate forensic completeness

Incident rapid playbook (network suspicion of exfil):
1) Quarantine suspect inference-subnet by applying deny-all egress rule (use documented API to avoid manual errors).
2) Snapshot and sign audit logs from last 48 hours; upload to evidence staging (mark as high-priority).
3) Issue temporary RBAC deny policy for principals with anomalous behavior (policy ID: emergency-block-YYYYMMDD).
4) Notify legal + CS team, and start formal incident packet (ticket JIRA-PD-842).

Appendix: sample queries and utilities
- Elastic DSL sample (mtls failures): {"query":{"bool":{"must":[{"match":{"mtls_verified":"false"}}],"range":{"@timestamp":{"gte":"now-24h"}}}}}
- Quick certificate check from control plane host: openssl s_client -connect inference-service:7443 -showcerts -verify 5
- Verify evidence manifest signature (pseudo): redwood-evidence-verify --manifest manifest.json --pubkey /etc/redwood/hsm_pub.pem

Open questions / follow-ups (for design review):
- Decide default leaf cert TTL for on-prem (8h vs 4h tradeoff).
- Define pragmatic encryption-in-transit exception list (third-party telemetry proxies).
- Complete integration test with customer-managed SIEM (elastic cloud + S3 retention).

References and links:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-1234 (RBAC v2 design doc)
- GitHub repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-mtls-ops (controller PR linked above)
- JIRA: JIRA-PD-842 (evidence automation epic)

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is a working draft; parts are intentionally prescriptive so customers get a repeatable baseline.
- Miguel: I pulled metrics port 9300 from our current infra plan — confirm with observability if that conflicts.
- Priya: please add expected OCSP URL and HSM key id values for the sample manifests.

End of doc.
